title: Sprint 2 — Task Model & Create/Read APIs
description: Design the Task database model and ModelSerializer, run migrations, and implement authenticated REST endpoints to create, list, and retrieve tasks.

tickets.title: TODO-004: Create Task Model and Serializer
tickets.description:
### Overview
Design the core task data entity and its corresponding Django REST Framework serializer. In `tasks/models.py`, declare the `Task` model containing fields for title, optional description, boolean completion status, automated timestamps, and a foreign key relation linking each task to its `owner` (Django's `User` model with `CASCADE` deletion). In `tasks/serializers.py`, implement `TaskSerializer` extending `serializers.ModelSerializer`. Mark `owner`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` as read-only fields so clients cannot tamper with task ownership during API payloads.

### Dependencies
- `TODO-001`: Initialize Django REST API Project.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `Task` model is declared in `tasks/models.py` with fields: `title` (CharField, max_length=200), `description` (TextField, blank=True), `is_completed` (BooleanField, default=False), `created_at` (DateTimeField, auto_now_add=True), `updated_at` (DateTimeField, auto_now=True), and `owner` (ForeignKey to `User`, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='tasks').
- [ ] Database migrations are created via `makemigrations` and applied to SQLite via `migrate` without errors.
- [ ] `TaskSerializer` is created in `tasks/serializers.py` with `model = Task` and `fields = ['id', 'title', 'description', 'is_completed', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'owner']`.
- [ ] `owner` is designated as a read-only field (e.g. `serializers.ReadOnlyField(source='owner.username')` or in `read_only_fields`).
- [ ] Serializer validates that `title` is non-empty and does not allow client payloads to override `owner` or timestamp values.

### Expected Deliverables
- `tasks/models.py` with `Task` model.
- `tasks/migrations/0001_initial.py` (or initial task migration).
- `tasks/serializers.py` with `TaskSerializer`.

### Evaluation Criteria
- Migration inspection confirms table schema and foreign key constraints.
- Serializer testing confirms `owner`, `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are read-only.
- Input validation correctly flags missing or blank `title`.
learning_objectives: Design relational database models in Django ORM with ForeignKey relations.
Implement DRF ModelSerializers for JSON serialization and deserialization.
Configure read-only fields to prevent client data spoofing.
Generate and apply schema migrations for REST APIs.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Define Task Model and Run Migrations
tasks.description: In `tasks/models.py`, declare `class Task(models.Model)` with `title`, `description`, `is_completed`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `owner = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='tasks')`. Run `makemigrations` and `migrate`.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Implement TaskSerializer with Read-Only Controls
tasks.description: In `tasks/serializers.py`, implement `class TaskSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer)`. Include all model fields and set `read_only_fields = ['id', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'owner']`. Expose `owner = serializers.ReadOnlyField(source='owner.username')`.

common_mistakes: Making 'owner' writable in the serializer, allowing malicious users to forge task ownership.
Forgetting on_delete=models.CASCADE on the ForeignKey field.
Omitting read_only_fields for timestamps and primary key.
hints: Use `owner = serializers.ReadOnlyField(source='owner.username')` to represent the owner as a username string in responses.
Verify migrations by running `python manage.py showmigrations tasks`.

solution.models_py:
from django.db import models
from django.contrib.auth.models import User

class Task(models.Model):
    owner = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='tasks')
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    description = models.TextField(blank=True)
    is_completed = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-created_at']

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title
solution.serializers_py:
from rest_framework import serializers
from .models import Task

class TaskSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    owner = serializers.ReadOnlyField(source='owner.username')

    class Meta:
        model = Task
        fields = ['id', 'title', 'description', 'is_completed', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'owner']
        read_only_fields = ['id', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'owner']

tickets.title: TODO-005: Implement Create Task API
tickets.description:
### Overview
Build the authenticated REST API endpoint for task creation. Clients issue a `POST /api/tasks/` request with a JSON payload containing `title` and optional `description`. In the view logic (using DRF's `ListCreateAPIView`, `ModelViewSet`, or custom `APIView`), enforce `permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]`. When saving the validated serializer instance, override `perform_create(self, serializer)` to automatically associate the authenticated user: `serializer.save(owner=self.request.user)`. Unauthenticated requests must be rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

### Dependencies
- `TODO-004`: Create Task Model and Serializer.
- `TODO-003`: Implement Login and Logout APIs.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Endpoint `POST /api/tasks/` accepts JSON payloads.
- [ ] Request must include a valid authentication token in the `Authorization` header (`Authorization: Token <key>`).
- [ ] Unauthenticated requests return HTTP 401 Unauthorized with `{"detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."}`.
- [ ] Required field `title` is validated; missing or whitespace-only title returns HTTP 400 Bad Request.
- [ ] On successful creation, the task is saved to SQLite with `owner` set to `request.user`.
- [ ] The API responds with HTTP 201 Created and the serialized task JSON object including `id`, `title`, `description`, `is_completed` (default `false`), `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `owner`.

### Expected Deliverables
- `tasks/views.py` containing task creation view logic.
- URL pattern for `POST /api/tasks/` registered in `todoproject/urls.py` or `tasks/urls.py`.

### Evaluation Criteria
- `POST /api/tasks/` without auth token returns HTTP 401.
- `POST /api/tasks/` with valid token and payload returns HTTP 201 Created.
- Database inspection verifies `task.owner_id == request.user.id`.
- Submitting `{"description": "test"}` (missing title) returns HTTP 400.
learning_objectives: Implement authenticated write operations using DRF permission classes (IsAuthenticated).
Override perform_create to inject request.user into model instances.
Handle JSON input validation and return HTTP 400 Bad Request on errors.
Return HTTP 201 Created with location and complete serialized resource data.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Task Creation View
tasks.description: Implement `TaskListCreateView(generics.ListCreateAPIView)` or `TaskViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet)`. Set `permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated]` and `serializer_class = TaskSerializer`. Override `perform_create(self, serializer)` with `serializer.save(owner=self.request.user)`.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Route Wiring and Validation
tasks.description: Map `POST /api/tasks/` in URL routing. Test task creation using Postman/curl with `Authorization: Token <token>` and JSON body `{"title": "Complete lab", "description": "Finish all 12 tickets"}`.

common_mistakes: Reading 'owner' from request.data instead of injecting request.user via perform_create.
Missing IsAuthenticated permission class, allowing anonymous users to create tasks with null owner.
Returning HTTP 200 instead of HTTP 201 Created upon successful resource creation.
hints: In generic class-based views, override: `def perform_create(self, serializer): serializer.save(owner=self.request.user)`.
Remember to pass `Authorization: Token <your_token>` in header during API testing.
DRF will automatically validate `max_length=200` and `blank=False` based on the model field definitions.

tickets.title: TODO-006: Implement List and Retrieve Task APIs
tickets.description:
### Overview
Implement read operations for tasks: listing a user's task collection (`GET /api/tasks/`) and retrieving a specific task by its primary key (`GET /api/tasks/<int:pk>/`). Both endpoints require authentication and must enforce strict user isolation: a student must ONLY see tasks they created. If a user has no tasks, `GET /api/tasks/` returns an empty JSON list `[]` with HTTP 200 OK. If a user attempts to retrieve a task ID that does not exist or belongs to another student, the API must return HTTP 404 Not Found.

### Dependencies
- `TODO-005`: Implement Create Task API.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `GET /api/tasks/` returns a JSON array of all tasks owned by the authenticated user with HTTP 200 OK.
- [ ] `GET /api/tasks/` strictly filters by `owner=request.user`; tasks belonging to other users are never included in the array.
- [ ] If the authenticated user has zero tasks, `GET /api/tasks/` returns HTTP 200 OK with payload `[]`.
- [ ] `GET /api/tasks/<int:pk>/` retrieves an individual task by ID and returns HTTP 200 OK with the serialized task object.
- [ ] Attempting to retrieve a task owned by another user returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
- [ ] Requesting a non-existent task ID returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
- [ ] Unauthenticated requests to either endpoint return HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

### Expected Deliverables
- `tasks/views.py` implementing list and retrieve logic (`get_queryset()` filtered by `owner=self.request.user`).
- URL routes for `GET /api/tasks/` and `GET /api/tasks/<int:pk>/`.

### Evaluation Criteria
- User isolation check: User A creating a task cannot see it appear in User B's `GET /api/tasks/` list.
- `GET /api/tasks/<pk>/` with cross-user ID returns HTTP 404.
- Unauthenticated request returns HTTP 401.
learning_objectives: Implement collection and member GET endpoints in Django REST Framework.
Filter querysets dynamically by request.user in get_queryset().
Maintain data privacy and multi-user isolation in RESTful APIs.
Return appropriate HTTP status codes (200 OK, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found).

tasks.title: Task 1 — Task Collection Listing Endpoint
tasks.description: In `tasks/views.py`, ensure `get_queryset(self)` filters `Task.objects.filter(owner=self.request.user)`. Wire `GET /api/tasks/` returning HTTP 200 OK with task array.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Task Detail Retrieve Endpoint
tasks.description: Implement `TaskDetailView(generics.RetrieveUpdateDestroyAPIView)` or `RetrieveAPIView` mapped to `/api/tasks/<int:pk>/`. Ensure `get_queryset(self)` scopes to `owner=self.request.user` so other users' tasks return HTTP 404.

common_mistakes: Returning Task.objects.all() in get_queryset(), leaking private tasks across different users.
Returning HTTP 404 when a user has no tasks, instead of returning an empty array [] with HTTP 200 OK.
Hardcoding user filter without checking request.user.is_authenticated.
hints: DRF's `generics.RetrieveAPIView` or `RetrieveUpdateDestroyAPIView` handles single object lookup and automatic 404 responses.
Test with two different user tokens to verify that neither can access the other's tasks.

    path('api/tasks/', TaskListCreateView.as_view(), name='task-list-create'),
    path('api/tasks/<int:pk>/', TaskDetailView.as_view(), name='task-detail'),
